question: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 mainly categorised the large-scale industries into __________ fragments.
solution:
The correct answer is __**four**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 categorized large-scale industries into **four** main fragments.
 
• This policy was the first comprehensive industrial policy statement by the Government of India, aiming to lay down the pattern of industrial development.
 
• The four categories were: industries with exclusive state monopoly, basic and strategic industries, industries requiring regulation and control, and other industries.
 
• This categorization was intended to balance the roles of the public and private sectors in the industrial development of the country.
 
• The resolution was a significant step in outlining the government's approach to industrial development in post-independence India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 aimed to promote a mixed economy where both public and private sectors would work together to achieve balanced industrial growth.
 
• It laid the foundation for subsequent industrial policies and was instrumental in shaping India's economic structure.
 
• The resolution also emphasized the importance of protecting small-scale industries and ensuring fair competition.
 
• It was followed by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, which further elaborated on the role of the public sector in industrial development.
 
• This policy framework was crucial in guiding India's industrial strategy during the early years of independence.
